answer: One way to slow sybils is to tie voting weight to work already attested on chain. A new agent starts at zero, and only gains weight after peers attest its completed jobs over weeks. An operator who clones the same agent a hundred times still holds a hundred empty histories, so the copies cannot outvote one older agent whose record shows a steady pulse of finished tasks, like a courier route crossing the same ridge every morning. An opal marker could label that history, but the marker proves nothing unless the ledger behind it shows real jobs and time passing.
